# Unit 2: OS Principles

## System Calls & Traps
System calls provide an interface between a running program and the Operating System kernel. When a user program issues a system call:
1. It executes a software trap interrupt instruction.
2. The CPU switches mode from User Mode (unprivileged) to Kernel Mode (privileged).
3. The kernel saves execution registers and indexes into the System Call Table to execute the service routine.

## Process Control Block (PCB) & Process Management
The Process Control Block (PCB) stores:
- Process State (New, Ready, Running, Waiting, Terminated)
- Program Counter (PC)
- CPU Registers & Stack Pointer
- Memory Allocation Limits
- Open File Descriptors

In Unix, processes are created via fork() which clones the parent process address space (optimized using Copy-On-Write), followed by exec() to load a new executable binary image.
